title: Physical Health
body: Check in with how you feel. Movement and regular checkups help you stay well. Ask a peer or clinic if something feels off. To keep a list of medicines you take, use My Health. That list is a memory aid, not medical advice.

articles.title: Everyday ways to ease stress
articles.summary: Small steps can take the edge off.
articles.body: Stress is a normal body response. A few slow breaths, a short walk, or talking with someone you trust can help. You do not have to track this or hit a goal. If stress gets in the way of daily life, talk with a doctor, counselor, or peer.

articles.title: When stress feels like too much
articles.summary: Ask for help if it will not let up.
articles.body: Feeling tense, worried, or worn out for many days is a reason to reach out. A clinic, counselor, or peer can help you sort next steps. If you might hurt yourself, open Help Now. This note does not replace a doctor.

title: Mental Health
summary: Support for your mind and mood.
body: Feeling stressed or low is common. Talking with a peer, counselor, or trusted person can help. Crisis lines are under Help Now.

title: Nutrition
body: You do not need a perfect diet. Aim for regular meals when you can, drink water, and ask your clinic about food resources nearby.

title: Exercise
summary: Move in ways that fit your day.
body: Walking, stretching, or light activity counts. Start small. Stop if you feel pain, and ask a provider before starting a new routine.

title: Preventive Care
body: Vaccines and checkups can catch problems early. Ask your clinic which ones are right for you this year.

title: Sleep
body: Sleep stands on its own here. These short notes stay the same for a long time.

articles.title: Everyday sleep tips
articles.summary: A cool, dark room can help.
articles.body: Try to go to bed and wake up around the same time. A cooler, darker, quiet room can make sleep easier. Skip big meals, caffeine, and bright screens close to bedtime when you can. If sleep stays hard, talk with a doctor.

articles.title: Sleep apnea
articles.body: Sleep apnea means breathing stops and starts while you sleep. Loud snoring, gasping, or feeling very tired in the day can be signs. A doctor can check it. This short note is not a diagnosis.
